source_text:
Ὅθεν καὶ

νόμος ἐγένετο ναύταις Φωκᾶν ἔχειν συνεστιάτορα. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ τὸν νῦν ἀσώματον
σύσσιτον εἶναι καὶ κοινωνὸν τραπέζης ἀμήχανον, μάθετε πῶς ἄρα φιλευσεβὴς
λογισμὸς ἐσοφίσατο τὸ ἀδύνατον. Καθ' ἑκάστην γὰρ τὴν ἡμέραν τὴν τῶν ὄψων
μερίδα πρὸς ἰσομοιρίαν τῶν ἐσθιόντων ἀποκληροῦσι τῷ μάρτυρι. Ταύτην δὲ εἷς τῶν
δαιτυμόνων ἐξωνούμενος τὸ ἀργύριον κατατίθεται, καὶ τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ ἄλλος καὶ
ἄλλοτε ἕτερος· καὶ οὗτος ὁ κλῆρος τῆς ἀγορασίας περιϊὼν ἅπαντας δίδωσι καθ'
ἡμέραν τῆς μερίδος τὸν ὠνητήν. Ἐπειδὰν δὲ ὅρμος αὐτοὺς ὑποδέξηται καὶ εἰς γῆν
ἀφίκωνται, μερίζεται τὸ ἀργύριον τοῖς πεινῶσι· καὶ τοῦτο ἡ μερὶς τοῦ Φωκᾶ,
πενήτων εὐεργεσία. Τεθήπασι τοῦτον καὶ βασιλεῖς τὸν καρτερικώτατον καὶ
φιλόθεον καὶ φιλοτίμοις κειμηλίοις κατακοσμοῦσι τοῦ περιβλέπτου πένητος τὸν
ναόν. Φιλονεικοῦσι δὲ οἱ ἐπιγινόμενοι τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους ὑπερβαλέσθαι. Καὶ οὔπω
θαυμαστόν, εἰ τῆς Ῥωμαίων ἡγεμονίας ἄνδρες φιλευσεβεῖς, θεσμοῖς καὶ νόμοις
σύντροφοι, οὕτως εὐλαβῶς ἔχουσι περὶ τὸν θεράποντα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁπότε καὶ εἰς
βαρβάρους ἔφθη τὸ θαῦμα· καὶ πάντες οἱ ἀγριώτατοι Σκύθαι, ὅσοι δὴ τὴν ἀντιπέρας
τοῦ Εὐξείνου πόντου ἤπειρον νέμονται, Μαιώτιδος λίμνης καὶ ποταμοῦ Τανάϊδος
πρόσοικοι, ὅσοι τε τὸν Βόσπορον οἰκοῦσι καὶ ἄχρι Φάσιδος ποταμοῦ παρατείνονται,
πάντες οὗτοι δορυφοροῦσι τῷ κηπουρῷ· τοῖς δὲ πᾶσιν ἔθεσι καὶ ἐπιτηδεύμασι
διεστῶτες ἡμῶν εἰς τοῦτο μόνον ὁμογνώμονες γίνονται τὴν ἀγριότητα τῶν τρόπων
9.126 ὑπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας ἐξημερούμενοι. Εἷς γοῦν ἄρχων ἐκεῖθεν καὶ βασιλεὺς τὸν
στέφανον τῆς κεφαλῆς ἀποθέμενος, χρυσῷ καὶ ἄνθεσι λίθων περιλαμπόμενον, καὶ
τὸν θώρακα τὸν πολεμικὸν ἀποδύς, ὕλας ἔχοντα πλούτου ἀλαζονικὴ γὰρ καὶ
θρυπτομένη τῶν βαρβάρων ἡ πανοπλία ἔπεμψεν ἀμφότερα ἀναθήματα διὰ τοῦ
μάρτυρος τῷ Θεῷ καὶ δυνάμεως καὶ ἀξιώματος καθιερώσας τὰς ἀφορμάς. Πρόδηλον
γάρ, ὡς ὁ μὲν στέφανος τῆς βασιλείας ἦν χαριστήριον, ὁ δὲ θώραξ τῆς κατὰ
πολέμους ἰσχύος. Τὰς δὲ συνεχῶς ἐπὶ τούτοις συμβαινούσας εὐεργεσίας διὰ τῶν ἐν
ὀνείρασιν ὄψεων καὶ διὰ τῶν θεραπειῶν, ὧν οἱ κάμνοντες ἀπολαύουσι, πῶς ἄν τις
καὶ διηγήσαιτο ἀδυνάτου καθεστῶτος ταῖς καθ' ἕκαστον ἐνεργείαις ἐπαφεῖναι τὸν
λόγον; Ἡμεῖς τοίνυν ἐνταῦθα λήξαντες δόξαν τῷ Σωτῆρι Θεῷ προσοίσομεν, οὗ
δοῦλοι πιστοὶ τοσαύτης ἠξιώθησαν χάριτος, ὥστε πρὸς πᾶσαν χρείαν καὶ περίστασιν
κατὰ τὴν δοθεῖσαν αὐτοῖς δωρεὰν τοὺς ὁμοδούλους εὐεργετεῖν. Καὶ ταῦτα μετὰ τὴν
ἐνθένδε ἄφιξιν καὶ τὸν τοῦ σώματος χωρισμόν· ὧν ἡ μνήμη μετὰ τοῦ ἔργου καθ'
3
ἡμέραν διατρέχει πόλεις καὶ κώμας πανταχοῦ τὸν εὐεργέτην κηρύσσουσα Κύριον, ᾧ
πρέπει πᾶσα τιμὴ καὶ κράτος, μεγαλοσύνη τε καὶ μεγαλοπρέπεια, νῦν καὶ ἀεί, καὶ εἰς
τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

thought_title: Phocas as table-companion of sailors and honored by barbarians
orientation: Asterius is closing the homily by describing the sailors' custom of setting aside a share for Phocas and the veneration of barbarian peoples, before ending with praise to God.
pass_a_gloss: From which also a custom became for sailors to have Phocas as table-companion. And since to have the now bodiless one as table-sharer and partner of the table is impossible, learn how then a God-loving reasoning devised the impossible. For each day they allot the portion of the dishes to the martyr for equal sharing of those eating. And this one of the banqueters buying it deposits the silver, and on the next day another and at another time a different one; and this lot of the purchase going around all gives each day the buyer of the portion. And whenever a harbor receives them and they arrive onto land, the silver is divided to the hungry; and this is the portion of Phocas, a benefaction of the poor. Kings also have marveled at this most steadfast and God-loving one and adorn with munificent treasures the church of the admired poor man. And those coming after strive to surpass the older ones. And not yet is it a wonder, if men of the Roman dominion, God-loving, reared with ordinances and laws, are thus reverently disposed toward the servant of Christ, when also to barbarians the wonder arrived; and all the most savage Scythians, as many as inhabit the mainland opposite the Black Sea, neighbors of the Sea of Azov and the Don River, and as many as dwell on the Bosporus and extend as far as the Phasis River, all these serve as bodyguards to the gardener; and though differing from us in all customs and practices, in this alone they become of one mind, the savagery of their ways being tamed by the truth. One ruler then from there and king, taking off the crown of his head, shining around with gold and flowers of stones, and stripping off the warlike breastplate, having materials of wealth—for boastful and delicate is the full armor of barbarians—sent both as offerings through the martyr to God, having consecrated the sources of power and dignity. For it is clear, that the crown was a thank-offering of the kingdom, and the breastplate of the strength in wars. And the benefits continually happening upon these through the visions in dreams and through the healings, which the sick enjoy, how could anyone even narrate, it being impossible to let the word touch upon the individual workings? We therefore, ceasing here, will offer glory to the Savior God, whose faithful servants were deemed worthy of so great a grace, as to benefit their fellow-servants for every need and circumstance according to the gift given to them. And these things after the departure from here and the separation of the body; whose memory with the deed runs through cities and villages each day, proclaiming everywhere the benefactor Lord, to whom is fitting all honor and might, majesty and magnificence, now and always, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The compound conveys sharing a meal together; 'table-companion' keeps the literal sense of eating together without importing a technical English term.
φιλευσεβής combines love and reverence; 'God-loving' preserves the compound's force and matches the glossary's reverence-for-God field.
The verb means to assign by lot; rendering it as 'allot by lot' keeps the lottery mechanism explicit, which matters for the custom described.
The verb literally means to attend as a spear-bearer or bodyguard; keeping the military image shows the honor given to the gardener by savage peoples.

choices.term: ἀλαζονικὴ γὰρ καὶ θρυπτομένη τῶν βαρβάρων ἡ πανοπλία
choices.english: for boastful and delicate is the full armor of barbarians
choices.why: The parenthetical comment explains why the breastplate has 'materials of wealth'; keeping the adjectives literal preserves the author's aside about barbarian ostentation.
rejected: for the full armor of barbarians is ostentatious and luxurious

choices.why: ἀφορμή means a starting-point or source; 'sources of power and dignity' keeps the metaphor that the crown and breastplate are the origins or instruments of royal authority.

pass_b_english: From this a custom arose among sailors: to have Phocas as their table-companion. And since it is impossible for him, now bodiless, to share their food and table, learn how God-loving reasoning found a way around the impossibility. Each day they allot by lot to the martyr a portion of the food, equal to the share of those who eat. One of the banqueters buys up that portion and deposits the money; the next day another does so, and at another time yet another. And this lot of purchase goes around among them all, giving each day a buyer for the portion. When a harbor receives them and they come to land, the money is divided among the hungry. This is Phocas's portion: a benefit to the poor.

Kings too have marveled at this most steadfast and God-loving man, and they adorn the church of this celebrated poor man with costly treasures. Those who come after strive to surpass their elders. And it is no wonder if men of the Roman empire, who love God and have been raised with its laws and customs, show such reverence for the servant of Christ, when the wonder has reached even barbarians. All the most savage Scythians—those who inhabit the mainland across the Black Sea, neighbors of the Sea of Azov and the Don River, and those who dwell along the Bosporus and stretch as far as the Phasis River—all these serve as bodyguards to the gardener. Though they differ from us in every custom and way of life, in this alone they become of one mind with us, their wildness of character tamed by the truth.

One ruler and king from that region, for example, took off the crown from his head, gleaming with gold and flowers of precious stones, and stripped off his war breastplate, which had materials of wealth—for boastful and delicate is the full armor of barbarians—and sent both as offerings through the martyr to God, consecrating the sources of his power and dignity. For it is clear that the crown was a thank-offering for his kingship, and the breastplate for his strength in wars.

As for the benefits that continually follow upon these—through visions in dreams and through the healings that the sick enjoy—how could anyone describe them, when it is impossible to apply words to each individual working? We, then, ending here, will offer glory to God the Savior, whose faithful servants were counted worthy of such grace that they benefit their fellow servants in every need and circumstance according to the gift given them. And this after their departure from here and the separation of the body. Their memory, together with their work, runs daily through cities and villages, everywhere proclaiming the benefactor Lord, to whom belongs all honor and power, greatness and majesty, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: the money is divided among the hungry. This is Phocas's portion: a benefit to the poor.
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ τοῦτο ἡ μερὶς τοῦ Φωκᾶ, πενήτων εὐεργεσία.
last_rejected.why: Source says 'and this is the portion of Phocas, a benefit to the poor' — the money divided IS Phocas's portion benefiting the poor, not a separate statement.
last_rejected.fix: the money is divided among the hungry; and this is Phocas's portion, a benefit to the poor.
last_rejected.ruling: English captures meaning: money divided IS Phocas's portion; colon and apposition clarify same idea as Greek.

last_rejected.why: περιβλέπτου modifies πένητος ('celebrated poor man'), but context is Phocas the celebrated poor man — 'this' is fine, but 'celebrated' should modify 'poor man' more clearly.
last_rejected.ruling: 'this celebrated poor man' correctly has 'celebrated' modifying 'poor man'; syntax and meaning are accurate.

last_rejected.why: ἄνθεσι means 'blossoms/flowers' as jewels set like flowers, not 'flowers of precious stones'
last_rejected.ruling: ἄνθεσι λίθων = 'flowers of stones'; 'flowers of precious stones' conveys the metaphor of jewels as flowers.

last_rejected.why: ὕλας πλούτου means 'materials of wealth' i.e. costly materials, but 'materials' is awkward; it means rich/wealthy materials
last_rejected.fix: rich with wealth's materials or wealth-laden
last_rejected.ruling: ὕλας ἔχοντα πλούτου = 'having materials of wealth'; 'materials of wealth' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: θρυπτομένη is 'effeminate/soft/luxurious,' not 'delicate' in a neutral sense; it's pejorative like 'pampered'
last_rejected.ruling: θρυπτομένη = 'delicate/soft/luxurious'; 'delicate' is within the word's range in context.

last_rejected.quote: consecrating the sources of his power and dignity
last_rejected.why: ἀφορμάς here means 'resources/occasions/causes,' not 'sources'; he consecrated the occasions/instruments of power
last_rejected.fix: consecrating the instruments of his power and rank
last_rejected.ruling: ἀφορμάς can mean 'resources/opportunities/occasions'; 'sources' is within acceptable range here.

last_rejected.why: χαριστήριον is 'thank-offering' but context shows it's the crown given as thanks for kingship, not 'for' kingship
last_rejected.fix: a thank-offering for his kingship (or: in gratitude for his rule)
last_rejected.ruling: χαριστήριον τῆς βασιλείας = 'thank-offering for kingship'; 'for' correctly conveys the genitive relationship.
